story:
Why this one matters: Following seven frenetic weeks of domestic club drama that saw Manchester City establish an unblemished 21-point lead and Tottenham Hotspur sink into crisis, the football calendar pivots to international competition for the October international window.

Headlining the slate in League A is a glamour encounter at Rome's Stadio Olimpico between Italy and Belgium. Luciano Spalletti's Azzurri have rebounded emphatically from a lackluster Euro 2024 campaign, taking maximum points in September with a statement 3-1 triumph in Paris over France followed by a gritty 2-1 win over Israel. Italy's midfield trio of Sandro Tonali, Samuele Ricci, and Davide Frattesi has injected verticality and pace into Spalletti's 3-5-1-1 setup.

Belgium arrive in the Italian capital facing a generational transition. With talisman Kevin De Bruyne nursing an injury and veteran striker Romelu Lukaku omitted to focus on fitness in Naples, Domenico Tedesco will entrust attacking responsibilities to RB Leipzig speedster Lois Openda and Manchester City winger Jeremy Doku. Elsewhere, England host Greece at Wembley looking to solidify promotion in League B, while South American squads begin crucial CONMEBOL World Cup qualifiers.
stakes: Nations League quarterfinal qualification seeding and FIFA World Ranking points ahead of the 2026 World Cup draw seeding.
rivalryAngle: Spalletti's rejuvenated Italy look to extend their psychological dominance over Belgium, having won their last three competitive meetings.
